keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria starts the row in -2200 and has it run to -2101 as one shape; the page dates the Memphite Seventh-Eighth Dynasties to c. 2181-c. 2160 BC. The page gives no territory for them (the shape stands, unverified); the only southern limit it gives is that the province of Siut 'acted as a buffer state between the northern and southern rulers' and lay 'in the south of the Heracleopolitan kingdom', which fits the shape's edge at lat 27.2. No infobox area on the page. Shape unchanged, years only.

union.text: the Heracleopolitan kingdom: the Delta and Middle Egypt south to Siut

correction.text: the Heracleopolitan kingdom ('Heracleopolis Magna (c. 2160 BC - c. 2050 BC)') with the Abydos region, where the Theban kings 'began the assault on the north'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's shape stops at Siut (lat 27.2) and omits Abydos (lat 26.2), but the page has Intef II 'begin the assault on the north, particularly at Abydos' and Intef III 'complete the conquest of Abydos, moving into Middle Egypt against the Heracleopolitan kings', so Abydos was northern land until the Theban conquest. The page does not say when the Heracleopolitans took Abydos; it is included for the whole Heracleopolitan phase (confidence 1).

correction.text: the Heracleopolitan kingdom after the loss of Abydos: the Delta and Middle Egypt south to Siut

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria runs this 74,134 km2 shape to -2001; the page has the north fall to Mentuhotep II 'around 2033 BC' (the infobox gives the period's end as c. 2055 BC and Heracleopolis as capital to c. 2050 BC; the page is not consistent). The shape stands for -2061..-2033 with Abydos gone to Thebes. Years cut at the end; shape unchanged. The page gives King Merikare (2065-2045 BC), later than the Theban end it lists.

region.text: the Delta and Middle Egypt, ruled from Memphis

ledger.note: c. 2181 BC: the Old Kingdom ends and the Memphite Seventh and Eighth Dynasties rule the north. Infobox 'Memphis (c. 2181 BC - c. 2160 BC), Seventh Dynasty-Eighth Dynasty'; the period 'spanned approximately 125 years, c. 2181 - c. 2055 BC'. The page names the capital, not the land; the Lower Egypt shape is Cliopatria's.

c. 2160 BC: the Ninth Dynasty takes over at Heracleopolis Magna. Infobox 'Heracleopolis Magna (c. 2160 BC - c. 2050 BC), Ninth Dynasty-Tenth Dynasty'; 'Akhthoes was described as a king who caused much harm to the inhabitants of Egypt'.
c. 2160 BC: the capital moves from Memphis to Heracleopolis Magna (Ihnasya el-Medina), in Lower Egypt.

region.text: Abydos, where Intef II 'begins the assault on the north'

ledger.note: c. 2069 BC: Thebes attacks the Abydos region. The page dates no assault: 'Intef II begins the assault on the north, particularly at Abydos'; the year is the start of Intef III's reign in the infobox ('c. 2069 BC - c. 2061 BC: Intef III'), who 'completed the conquest of Abydos'.
c. 2061 BC: the Abydos fighting ends in a Theban victory (Thebes 'c. 2134 BC - c. 2061 BC').

region.text: Abydos, 'the conquest of Abydos, moving into Middle Egypt'

ledger.note: c. 2061 BC: Intef III takes Abydos from the Heracleopolitans. Page: 'His successor, Intef III, completed the conquest of Abydos, moving into Middle Egypt against the Heracleopolitan kings.' Undated; placed at the end of the Theban Eleventh Dynasty's c. 2061 BC date. Siut stays northern: it 'acted as a buffer state'.

region.text: Siut and Middle Egypt, 'a buffer state between the northern and southern rulers'

ledger.note: c. 2055 BC: Mentuhotep II's war against Heracleopolis begins on the Siut borderland. The page dates no campaign of his; the year is his accession in the Middle Kingdom page (2055 BC), after Intef III had 'moved into Middle Egypt'.
c. 2033 BC: the war ends with Mentuhotep II's victory 'around 2033 BC'.

region.text: the Heracleopolitan kingdom, the Delta and Middle Egypt south to Siut

ledger.note: c. 2033 BC: Mentuhotep II defeats the Heracleopolitan kings and Egypt is reunited. Page: he 'would eventually defeat the Heracleopolitan kings around 2033 BC and unify the country. This event marked the beginning of the Middle Kingdom of Egypt.' The Middle Kingdom page instead puts his accession in 2055 BC.

region.text: the Heracleopolitan kingdom, passing to the Theban Middle Kingdom

ledger.note: c. 2033 BC: the northern kingdom ends with the Theban conquest.

wars.name: Theban-Heracleopolitan war

zones.text: Siut, 'a buffer state between the northern and southern rulers'

wars.outcome: The Theban Eleventh Dynasty took Abydos (Intef III) and 'moving into Middle Egypt'; Mentuhotep II 'would eventually defeat the Heracleopolitan kings around 2033 BC and unify the country'.
wars.note: 'Rule of Egypt was roughly equally divided between two competing power bases.' The page dates only the start of Intef III's reign (c. 2069 BC), the Theban end (c. 2061) and the final defeat (around 2033 BC); no battle is dated, and the Siut borderland is not shown to have changed hands before 2033.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey borders; the northern kingdom is Cliopatria's Delta-and-Middle-Egypt shape, with the Siut buffer in the south (page) and Abydos disputed from c. 2069 BC.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Lower Egypt' (-2200..-2001, two shapes of 74.5k and 74.1k km2) is the northern kingdom of the First Intermediate Period: Memphite Seventh-Eighth Dynasties to c. 2160 BC, then the Heracleopolitan Ninth-Tenth Dynasties. This dossier IS the 'rival Herakleopolis' the group scope says Cliopatria lacks; me-03-x need not write it. Dates follow the page (c. 2181 to the Theban conquest around 2033 BC) against Cliopatria's -2200..-2001; the shape beyond -2033 belongs to the Middle Kingdom. PAGE CONFLICTS: the First Intermediate Period page ends the period c. 2055 BC and Heracleopolis c. 2050 BC, lists Merykare last Heracleopolitan king in c. 2069-2061, yet dates the defeat 'around 2033 BC' and Mentuhotep II's stela 'ca. 2051-2030'; the Middle Kingdom page has Mentuhotep II 'ascended the Theban throne in 2055 BC'. The end is set at the one explicit defeat date, -2033. The page also lists Intef III (c. 2069-2061) as Intef II's successor while dating Intef II's defeat of Nekhen 'by around 2060'. No territory is given for the Memphite Seventh-Eighth Dynasties (c. 2181-2160 BC); the shape is Cliopatria's. The page gives no Delta event beyond 'Kheti III ... bring some degree of order to the Delta', and nothing on Asiatics or Nubia. Gazetteer names needed: Heracleopolis Magna (Ihnasya el-Medina; coordinates given in capitals), Middle Egypt (region).
